Bachelor’s degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.

At least seven years of progressive and successful experience in an executive assistant role, preferably at UC, performing a range of administrative functions including complex scheduling, logistical arrangements in a high-profile environment; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
The Executive Assistant 4 (EA4) serves as a high-level administrative officer within the Office of the Secretary and Chief of Staff to the Regents. The incumbent is responsible for:
50% — Executive Operations & Calendar Management

Handling with precision the day-to-day scheduling, complex calendaring, and operational logistics for members of the Board of Regents, the Secretary and Chief-of-Staff (SCOS), and executive leadership within the Office;
Complex Scheduling: Manage the calendars for members of the Board of Regents and executive staff within the SCOS, balancing multiple competing priorities and time-sensitive requests.
Coordinating regental engagements with both internal and external stakeholders, including but not limited to meeting and event logistics and travel planning;

Operational Coordination: Utilize collaborative work management systems (e.g., Asana, Smartsheet) and content management platforms (e.g., Google Workspace, Box, Cascade CMS) to coordinate Board meetings, briefings, and other meetings involving Regents and the SCOS.
Serving as a liaison between Regents and senior university leaders (e.g., UCOP executives and campus chancellors) to coordinate meetings on behalf of the Secretary and Chief of Staff;

Fiscal & Confidential Administration: Handle sensitive governance and personnel materials with the highest level of discretion in support of office operations. Utilize institutional financial and travel systems (e.g., Concur) to process expense reports, track vendor payments, and ensure strict compliance with UC policy.
Preparing and curating meeting and event materials in a timely manner; and

Travel and Logistics Support: Serve as backup to the Business Manager by coordinating complex travel arrangements, processing travel reimbursements for the 26-member Board, and overseeing related logistical support.
Supporting the administrative and clerical needs of the SCOS Office.
30% — Meeting & Event Coordination
This role requires an understanding of UC governance, political acumen, and the ability to professionally manage confidential fiscal and HR matters.

Stakeholder Coordination: Serve as the primary administrative liaison among Regents, senior administration (including UCOP leaders, Chancellors, and Principal Officers), and internal teams to ensure alignment on meeting logistics and scheduling.
This position reports directly to the Secretary and Chief of Staff to the Regents.

Document Control & Tracking: Maintain centralized repositories for engagement-related materials, including briefing documents and background materials; proactively track cross-departmental deliverables to ensure timely distribution for Regental review.

Travel & Logistics Management: Make intricate travel arrangements, including airfare and ground transportation, while conducting cost-benefit analyses to ensure fiscal responsibility and efficient travel planning.
Meeting & Event Support: Support the planning and execution of Regents meetings and events by coordinating attendee management, seating arrangements, name badges, table tents, and admit lists.
20% — Administrative Support

Financial Administration & Compliance: Support the management of expense tracking and complex travel reimbursements through financial and travel platforms. Ensure all purchases, invoices, and transactions are processed in strict accordance with UC policies.
HR & Recruitment Support: Facilitate the STEP and annual performance evaluation process and assist staff with administrative HR procedures and deadline requirements.

Facilities & ITS Coordination: Support operational needs related to space planning, facilities coordination, and ITS services for the office. Maintain listservs, call directories, and electronic records management systems.
Performs other duties as assigned and complies with all University policies, procedures, and professional standards.
